correctness.rationale: Using the source definitions \(r_n=\omega_{n-1}/\omega_{n-2}\), strict gamma log-convexity yields \(r_n>\sqrt{2\pi/n}>\sqrt{6/n}\). Elementary forward-difference arguments imply \(B_n<1/\sqrt n\) for \(n\ge3\) and \(B_n<1/(2\sqrt n)\) for \(n\ge14\). The duplication formula and elementary parity bounds on \(\Gamma(n/2+1)\) give \(A_n>1/(2\sqrt n)\) all \(n\ge2\). The remaining \(3\le n\le13\) have an exact rational lower bound using \(3<\pi<22/7\) and \(\sqrt3<7/4\); an independent integer-fraction reimplementation checked all 11 cases, with smallest normalized ratio \(1944365472/1771561>1000\) at \(n=3\). At \(n=2\), \(A_2^6=4\pi/3>1=B_2^6\). Thus the bound genuinely covers the infinite tail and every finite boundary. The paper\'s Lemma A.2 gives the stated equivalence to branch selection; no assertion about optimal constants is made.
